encryption_key_rbac_audit_enforcement.encryption_at_rest: DISABLED by default (config.yaml:16-19, code-traced). Pseudonymization is not encryption -- data at rest is plaintext with re-linkable-with-key pseudonyms, not ciphertext.
encryption_key_rbac_audit_enforcement.key_custody: HMAC key is a 0600-mode sidecar file; PHIKeyStore holds it in a zeroizable bytearray singleton; llm-agent role is denied access at two enforcement layers (phi_scrub.py + phi_keystore.py). Missing key forfeits re-derivation of prior pseudonyms (documented irreversibility lever).

encryption_key_rbac_audit_enforcement.rbac: DISABLED by default (config.yaml:25-26). The only enforced role gate in code is the llm-agent key-access denial (phi_scrub.py:335-343), not a general RBAC system.

date_shift_inference.bounded_outcome: This is the same disclosed re-identification vector documented for interval-preserving date-shift methods generally (NIST SP 800-188 Section 4.3.12 candidate failure modes); it is why Safe Harbor requires generalization to year, not shift-preserving transforms.
date_shift_inference.finding: SANT date-shift preserves inter-visit intervals per subject (code-traced, measured 56/56 interval-preserved in docs/JURISDICTION_EVIDENCE_REPORT_US.md). An attacker who knows the true date of ANY single event for a subject (e.g. a public admission date) can recover the per-subject offset and therefore every other shifted date for that subject, since the offset is constant across all of that subject's dates.

hmac_pseudonymization.bounded_outcome: Re-identification requires either (a) key compromise (full reversal) or (b) a known-plaintext/frequency attack correlating deterministic tokens across releases -- both are documented, expected properties of keyed pseudonymization, not surprises.
hmac_pseudonymization.finding: pseudo_id() is deterministic per (label, raw_id, key): the SAME raw identifier under the SAME label always produces the SAME RID_<LABEL>_<alpha12> token (phi_scrub.py:1345-1374, code-traced this session). An attacker holding a known (raw_id, pseudonym) pair and the ability to query the pipeline with chosen raw_ids can confirm linkage for other records without needing the key. This is inherent to deterministic keyed pseudonymization (not a bug) and is exactly why the current system does not and cannot claim HIPAA Safe Harbor for jitter_date/pseudonymize (see repository trace section 2.7).

linkage_reidentification_attacks.methodology: NIST SP 800-188 Section 4.3.12 potential-failure-mode framework (see reg-0033); this repo's own deterministic MIA smoke test retained only as a smoke test per KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md, not external validation.

quasi_identifier_linkage.bounded_outcome: Confirmed structural gap for free-text quasi-identifier combinations; structured/tabular quasi-identifier risk is covered by the existing k-anon gate (not independently re-benchmarked this session).
quasi_identifier_linkage.finding: harness/make_privacy_gateway_fixtures.py 'text-quasi-identifier-006' plants exactly this combination as a single free-text record. Neither phi_engine's header-level scrub config nor its regex/checksum detection catalog performs cross-field quasi-identifier risk scoring on free text; the k-anonymity gate (kanon_gate.py/pycanon_gate.py) operates on STRUCTURED/tabular data, not narrative text, so this specific free-text combination is NOT covered by any current control.
